body_text: Bootstrap admin templates are pre-designed backend user interfaces built on the Bootstrap framework that give developers a complete starting point for dashboards, internal tools, and business applications. Instead of spending weeks wiring up sidebars, data tables, forms, and chart widgets from scratch, you get a tested, fully responsive layout with a rich component library - and you focus your engineering time on domain logic. This guide compares the leading bootstrap admin template options available in 2026, breaks down the features that actually matter, and helps you decide whether a template, a platform, or a custom build is the right call for your project. What Are Bootstrap Admin Templates A bootstrap admin dashboard template is a pre-built UI framework layered on top of Bootstrap (most commonly Bootstrap 5.3 in 2026) that bundles styled components - navigation bars, data grids, forms, chart widgets, notification widgets - along with layout scaffolding for sidebars, headers, and content areas. These templates provide ready-to-use structural layouts for dashboards and admin areas, allowing developers to skip repetitive front-end work and ship production interfaces faster. Using a bootstrap admin template can significantly reduce development time. Rather than building responsive layouts, theming, and dozens of UI elements from zero, developers start with a proven foundation that handles responsive design across desktops, tablets, and mobile devices. The Bootstrap framework itself provides battle-tested grid systems, bootstrap utility classes, and browser compatibility across major browsers - templates extend all of this with domain-specific components like analytics dashboards, authentication pages, and CRUD interfaces. The ecosystem in 2026 is mature and competitive. Many top-tier templates are built with Bootstrap 5 and have no jQuery dependency, using vanilla JavaScript or TypeScript instead. Templates now routinely ship with dark mode and light mode support, RTL layouts, CSS custom properties for theming, and framework-specific versions for React, Vue, and Angular. Common use cases for bootstrap admin templates include CRM systems and analytics dashboards, SaaS products, e-commerce admin panels, and internal business tools. Developers choose bootstrap admin over building from scratch for several practical reasons: faster development cycles, consistent and professional UI across applications, tested responsive behavior across different devices, and the ability to customize templates to match specific branding requirements without needing advanced design skills. Types of Bootstrap Admin Templates Bootstrap admin templates break down into four meaningful categories, each suited to different project needs, budgets, and team compositions. Free Open Source Templates A free bootstrap admin template - typically released under an MIT license - gives you a solid baseline at zero cost. Templates like AdminLTE and CoreUI's free version offer many features: responsive layouts, pre-built pages, basic chart widgets, data tables, and forms. They're backed by large communities, which means active issue tracking, community plugins, and plenty of tutorials. The trade-off is predictable: free templates may lack complex components, enterprise-grade support, and some advanced UI elements. Updates can arrive more slowly, and you won't get bundled premium plugins or dedicated help channels. But for MVPs, internal tools, and projects with tight budgets, a free bootstrap admin template is often more than sufficient. Premium Commercial Templates Premium admin dashboard templates add enhanced component libraries, professional support, more components and layout options, and frequent updates. They typically cost between $29–$79 per license and include pre-built page layouts for specific use cases - invoicing, project management, user management, file managers - along with priority support channels. The investment makes sense when your team needs polished, production-ready interfaces with guaranteed maintenance, when you're building commercial projects that demand a professional admin theme, or when you need enterprise features like advanced theming, multiple layout variants, and comprehensive documentation. Framework-Specific Templates Rather than shipping only HTML/CSS/JS, many admin templates now offer native implementations for React, Vue, Angular, and Laravel. Framework-specific versions include proper state management, routing integration, and component wrappers that feel native to each ecosystem. CoreUI stands out here by offering native implementations of its UI library for React, Vue, Angular, and pure Bootstrap - all sharing the same API and design system. Metronic similarly supports Bootstrap, React, Angular, Vue, and Laravel. If your team already works in a specific framework, choosing a template with native support eliminates the integration overhead of adapting a plain HTML template to your stack. Industry-Focused Templates Specialized templates target specific domains - e-commerce, healthcare, fintech, analytics - and ship with pre-built components tailored to those use cases. Think order management tables, financial charts, patient intake forms, compliance interfaces, and audit log viewers. Premium templates like Metronic include dozens of demo apps (file manager, invoice, projects, accounts) ready for adaptation. If your project has specific business needs, an industry-focused template can save weeks of component development compared to starting with a generic admin dashboard. What to Look For in Bootstrap Admin Templates Rich component libraries are critical to ensure extensive UI options in templates. But beyond component count, several key attributes determine whether a template will serve your project well or become technical debt. Data Integration Capabilities Admin panels exist to manage data. The best templates provide out-of-the-box support for data tables with pagination, sorting, and search; form validation (client-side and server-bound controls); file upload managers; and structures that map cleanly to API endpoints. AdminLTE v4, for example, includes Tabulator-based data tables and sample apps like Kanban and File Manager that demonstrate real data integration patterns. Look for templates where the data layer is architected to connect to your backend - not just styled static mockups. UI Components and Design System Evaluate the depth of the component library: multi-select dropdowns, date range pickers, steppers, chips, modals, toast notifications, and more. Bootstrap templates typically come with UI components like charts, forms, and notification widgets - but quality varies widely. Key indicators include: Theming flexibility - Sass variables, CSS custom properties, custom CSS override paths Responsive design - truly mobile-first, fluid grids tested across screen size breakpoints Dark mode and light themes - native support via data-bs-theme, not a bolted-on afterthought Design consistency - bootstrap components that feel cohesive, not a patchwork of third-party plugins CoreUI's component library demonstrates strong variety with custom elements like chip sets, multi-selects, and steppers that extend beyond raw Bootstrap defaults. Security and Authentication While template code doesn't enforce backend security, good templates include well-structured authentication pages for login, registration, password reset, and role/permission UI controls. Many templates include built-in authentication pages for user management, providing the front-end scaffolding you need to wire up to your auth backend. AdminLTE v4 added an accessibility module targeting WCAG 2.1 AA compliance, with ARIA labeling and keyboard navigation - features that increasingly overlap with security considerations like accessible error messaging and secure form validation patterns. Developer Experience Documentation and regular maintenance are important features of good Bootstrap templates. Beyond that, evaluate: Clean code and well commented code - modular architecture, organized folder structure, logical naming Build tooling - npm/pnpm support, modern bundlers (Vite, Webpack 5), SCSS/Pug pipelines JavaScript source files - vanilla JS or TypeScript, minimal jquery dependency Customization - ability to override styles, swap components, and extend without forking the entire codebase Migration paths - documentation for upgrading between template versions A developer friendly template saves time not just at setup but throughout the project lifecycle. AdminLTE v4's rewrite includes layout blueprints, migration guides, and vanilla JS modules. CoreUI offers AI-assisted scaffolding and framework bindings. How to Choose the Right Bootstrap Admin Template Turn the features above into a practical decision framework: Project complexity and timeline - For a quick internal tool or prototype, a free template with pre-built pages gets you to production in days. For a customer-facing SaaS product, invest in a premium or framework-specific template with deeper component coverage and long-term support. Team technology stack - If your team builds in React or Vue, choose templates with native framework versions. Adapting a pure HTML template to a component-based framework creates unnecessary friction and technical debt. Budget and support needs - Free admin templates cover most UI needs for internal tools. Premium versions justify their cost when you need guaranteed support, advanced layouts, and components for commercial projects. Evaluate whether the premium tier's extra features actually match your requirements - don't pay for components you won't use. Long-term maintenance - Check commit frequency, release history, and community activity. Some well-known templates have stalled: Material Dashboard's free npm package, for instance, hasn't seen a release in years and carries low maintenance scores . Active maintenance isn't optional for production web apps. Scalability and integration - Modular architecture, an organized folder structure, and clean separation of concerns make it possible to grow with your project. Templates that tightly couple styles, logic, and layout become painful to scale. Top Bootstrap Admin Templates for 2026 Each template below was evaluated on component depth, framework support, maintenance activity, documentation quality, accessibility, and community adoption. Here's how they compare: Template Bootstrap Version jQuery Dependency Framework Versions License Dark Mode AdminLTE 5.3 None HTML (primary) MIT Yes CoreUI 5 None React, Vue, Angular MIT / Pro Yes Material Dashboard 5 None HTML, React MIT / Pro Limited SB Admin 5 None HTML MIT Basic Metronic 5 None React, Vue, Angular, Laravel Commercial Yes ArchitectUI 5 Minimal HTML Free / Pro Yes AdminLTE AdminLTE was first released in December 2013 and has since become one of the most widely adopted free bootstrap admin templates in the world. It has over 45,000 GitHub stars and has been downloaded over 8.5 million times. It is used by developers in over 180 countries. The latest version (v4.0.0, released May 2026) is a ground-up rewrite built on Bootstrap 5.3 with zero jquery dependency - everything runs on vanilla TypeScript. AdminLTE includes 18+ built-in plugins and ships with demo apps for chat, calendar, file manager, kanban, and more. Six built-in skins use CSS custom properties for seamless dark mode switching via the data-bs-theme attribute. The accessibility module targets WCAG 2.1 AA with keyboard navigation and ARIA labeling. Best for: Teams that want a highly customizable, free, community-backed template for dashboards and internal tools. The MIT license allows use in commercial projects without restrictions. Limitations: Primarily an HTML template - framework-specific versions are less mature. No bundled backend logic or premium plugin packages in the free version. CoreUI CoreUI is built on Bootstrap 5 for modern responsive design and stands out for its multi-framework approach. CoreUI supports multiple frameworks like Angular and React, with native implementations that share a unified API and design system. CoreUI includes pre-built widgets and UI components - including new components like chip sets, improved NavGroup, and search buttons added in mid-2026 releases. CoreUI is lightweight and performance-oriented for fast loading. CoreUI is open source with enterprise-level support available in premium tiers. Themes are built with Sass Modules and support RTL layouts using CSS logical properties. Best for: Teams working across multiple frameworks who want a consistent component library. The free version covers most use cases; the Pro version adds advanced ui elements and enterprise features. Limitations: Full component suite requires a premium license. Enterprise-grade features are gated behind paid tiers. Material Dashboard Material Dashboard is inspired by Google's Material Design and applies material design principles to Bootstrap admin interfaces. The free version includes basic bootstrap components, color filters, and demo pages for maps, tables, and user profiles. Best for: Projects that need a clean, modern design aligned with Google's design language. Suitable for simple web apps, proof-of-concept dashboards, or projects where material design consistency matters. Limitations: Maintenance is a concern - the free npm package hasn't seen significant updates in years. Community activity has declined. Not recommended for enterprise projects needing long-term support or frequent security patches. SB Admin SB Admin is a free bootstrap admin dashboard template built on Bootstrap 5 that provides a clean starting point for simple admin panels. It includes basic layouts, charts, data tables, and forms with a straightforward organized folder structure. Best for: Developers who want a minimal, lightweight starting point without the overhead of large template ecosystems. Good for learning, prototyping, or small internal tools. Limitations: Fewer pre-built pages and components compared to AdminLTE or CoreUI. Limited plugin ecosystem and less active community support. Metronic Metronic is a premium admin dashboard template with over 120,000 sales as of June 2026. Metronic supports Bootstrap, React, Angular, Vue, and Laravel, making it one of the most comprehensive multi-framework options available. It includes pre-built page layouts for accounts, projects, e-commerce, file management, and more, along with multiple layout options and RTL support. Best for: Enterprise teams and commercial projects that need a polished, feature-rich admin theme with professional support and regular updates. The breadth of framework support and pre-built pages makes it strong for complex web applications. Limitations: Commercial license (~$49 for a regular license). The template is large and can have a steeper learning curve. Customizing heavily may require significant effort to strip unused features, and unused components can add overhead if not properly tree-shaken. ArchitectUI ArchitectUI HTML includes multiple pre-built dashboards and offers a visually distinctive approach to admin panel design. The free tier provides solid coverage for basic admin needs, while premium versions unlock additional layouts, page templates, and more components. Best for: Developers who want a visually differentiated admin dashboard without extensive custom CSS work. The free version works well for smaller projects; premium tiers suit teams that need broader component variety. Limitations: Smaller community compared to AdminLTE or CoreUI. Some legacy jquery dependency in older versions. Less documentation depth than the market leaders. Bootstrap Templates vs Admin Platforms Bootstrap admin templates solve the front-end problem - they give you responsive layouts, ui components, and pre-built pages. But they don't solve the full-stack problem. You still need to build or integrate: Backend API endpoints and data connections Authentication and authorization logic Role-based access control (beyond UI mockups) Audit logging and compliance features Deployment infrastructure and hosting There are three approaches to building admin panels, each with distinct trade-offs: Approach Development Time Flexibility Maintenance Burden Build from scratch Weeks–months Maximum High Bootstrap template Days–weeks High (front-end) Medium Admin platform Hours–days Moderate Low A platform like Jet Admin takes a fundamentally different approach. Instead of providing UI scaffolding that you wire to a backend, Jet Admin connects directly to your existing databases, APIs, spreadsheets, and SaaS tools - generating the interface and application logic, then deploying the app to users. It supports 50+ data sources including PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Firebase, Stripe, HubSpot, and REST/GraphQL APIs. Where bootstrap templates give you authentication pages as static HTML, Jet Admin provides actual governance: role-based access control down to rows, columns, and actions; SSO/SAML/SCIM integration; audit logs; and branded custom-domain deployment. For teams that need a governed admin experience on top of existing infrastructure - rather than building that governance layer themselves - a platform approach can deliver better ROI, especially for saas platforms and enterprise use cases. For self-hosted requirements, Jet Bridge (open-source, MIT-licensed) runs on your infrastructure and exposes your SQL database to the Jet Admin frontend via an auto-generated REST API - data transmits directly between the browser and your server without passing through Jet Admin's cloud. Implementation and Deployment Considerations Once you've selected a template, the implementation path matters as much as the choice itself: Development workflow: Start by auditing the template's organized folder structure and removing unused components. Configure your build pipeline (npm/pnpm, Vite or Webpack) and set up Sass variable overrides rather than modifying source files directly - this protects your customizations during future updates. Team collaboration: Establish conventions for custom CSS overrides, component extensions, and javascript source files organization. Version-control the template alongside your application code, and document any modifications to core template files. Testing: Verify responsive behavior across screen sizes and major browsers. Test dark mode, light themes, and RTL layouts if your users need them. Validate accessibility (keyboard navigation, screen reader compatibility) early - retrofitting is expensive. Deployment: Most bootstrap templates are static front-end assets that deploy to any hosting environment - CDN, S3, Netlify, or your own servers. If you're using framework-specific versions (React, Vue), your deployment pipeline follows standard SPA or SSR patterns. Consider bundle size: strip unused plugins and components to keep load times fast. Maintenance planning: Pin your template version and track upstream releases. Templates with active maintenance (AdminLTE, CoreUI) publish changelogs and migration guides. Templates with low maintenance (Material Dashboard) require you to absorb that maintenance burden yourself - patching security issues, updating dependencies, and fixing browser compatibility problems. Frequently Asked Questions What's the difference between free and premium bootstrap admin templates? Free bootstrap admin templates (like AdminLTE under MIT license) provide core layouts, essential ui components, and basic pre-built pages - enough for most internal tools and prototypes. Premium versions add more components, advanced layouts, dedicated support channels, additional pre-built page layouts, and often include premium plugins for charts, data tables, and file management. The choice depends on whether your project needs those extras and whether you value guaranteed support and updates. How do I integrate a bootstrap template with my existing database? Bootstrap templates are front-end only - they provide the UI layer but don't include backend data connections. You'll need to build API endpoints that your template's forms, data tables, and dashboards consume. Framework-specific template versions (React, Vue, Angular) integrate more naturally with state management and API calls. Alternatively, platforms like Jet Admin connect directly to databases and APIs without requiring you to build that middleware. Can bootstrap admin templates handle enterprise-level security requirements? Templates provide the UI scaffolding for security features - login forms, role selection interfaces, permission toggles - but don't enforce backend security. Enterprise-grade authentication, role-based access control, audit logging, and SSO require backend implementation. AdminLTE v4's accessibility module and WCAG 2.1 AA compliance address the front-end accessibility side. For full governance without custom backend work, consider admin platforms that include these capabilities natively. What's the typical development time for implementing a bootstrap admin template? A basic admin dashboard using a free template can be functional in 1–3 days for simple use cases. A fully customized, production-ready web application with integrated backend, custom branding, and tested responsive layouts typically takes 2–6 weeks depending on complexity. Framework-specific versions with proper API integration sit on the longer end. Using a template still significantly reduces development time compared to building from scratch. When should I consider an admin platform instead of a bootstrap template? Consider a platform when you need rapid deployment (hours, not weeks), built-in governance features (role-based access, audit logs, SSO), connections to multiple data sources without building middleware, or when your team lacks the front-end engineering bandwidth to customize and maintain a template long-term. Templates make more sense when you need maximum UI flexibility, have specific design requirements, or want full control over every aspect of the front-end code. How do I customize a bootstrap template without breaking future updates? Use the template's intended customization layer: override Sass variables rather than editing source files, extend components through the template's plugin architecture, and keep custom CSS in separate files. Maintain an organized folder structure that separates your customizations from template core files. Pin your template version, review changelogs before upgrading, and use version control to track exactly what you've changed. Templates with well commented code and clear documentation (like AdminLTE and CoreUI) make this process significantly easier. Making Your Decision Choosing the right bootstrap admin template comes down to matching your project's actual requirements - not picking the template with the longest feature list. For internal tools and MVPs , a free bootstrap admin template like AdminLTE or CoreUI's free version delivers faster development with zero licensing cost. For commercial products and enterprise apps , premium options like Metronic or CoreUI Pro provide the polish, support, and component depth that production web apps demand. For teams that need governed admin experiences without building backend infrastructure , a platform approach like Jet Admin eliminates the gap between UI templates and production-ready admin panels. Start by mapping your must-have features against the comparison table above. Test your top two candidates with a real page from your application - not just the demo. And prioritize active maintenance: the best-looking template today becomes a liability tomorrow if it stops receiving updates. These templates offer a consistent and professional UI across applications - your job is to pick the one that fits your stack, your timeline, and your team.

title: Battalion Oil Announces Refinancing and Execution of Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement
summary: Battalion Oil strengthens balance sheet through Fortress refinancing, securing a fixed 6.50% SOFR margin and enhancing liquidity flexibility through 2029...
body_text: Houston, Texas, July 01, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Battalion Oil Corporation (NYSE American: BATL, “Battalion” or the “Company”) today announced the closing of a refinancing of its senior secured credit facility through the execution of a Third Amended and Restated Senior Secured Credit Agreement (the “New Credit Agreement”), which reduces borrowing costs, extends debt maturity through December 2029, defers principal amortization, and provides potential access to additional discretionary capital to support the Company's ongoing operations and strategic objectives. Key Highlights Achieved improved terms with no new cash borrowing and no novation, as existing lenders rolled the full $162.5 million of outstanding term loans into the New Credit Agreement, emphasizing continued lender confidence in Battalion’s credit. Net debt as of June 29, 2026 is ~$65.5 million; total gross term loan debt of $162.5 million less ~$96.99 million of cash and reinvestment proceeds. Reduced borrowing costs by a minimum of 125 basis points, replacing the Existing Credit Agreement's leverage-based pricing grid of 7.75% to 8.50% with a fixed applicable margin of 6.50% over SOFR. Extended debt maturity by a full year from December 26, 2028 to December 31, 2029. Deferred all principal amortization for a full year, with scheduled quarterly payments under the New Credit Agreement not commencing until the fiscal quarter ending June 30, 2027. Secured access to up to $175 million of additional discretionary delayed draw capacity to fund future growth, available on an uncommitted basis. Management Comments The refinancing strengthens Battalion's capital structure by reducing borrowing costs, extending debt maturities, and enhancing liquidity flexibility for future development activities. These improvements build on the Company's balance sheet initiatives completed earlier in 2026, including the divestiture of the West Quito Assets and the associated debt reduction from approximately $208.1 million at year-end 2025 to approximately $162.5 million as of March 31, 2026, as previously reported, and further position Battalion to execute its Monument Draw development program and long-term strategic objectives. Given the significant cash on hand and reinvestment proceeds, the Company has ample liquidity to execute on its favorable Joint Development Agreement with enhanced economics as well as additional accretive operations or strategic alternatives. “Closing this refinancing is a meaningful milestone for Battalion,” said Matt Steele, Chief Executive Officer of Battalion. “Locking in a fixed 6.50% margin over SOFR reduces our borrowing costs and eliminates the uncertainty associated with a leverage-based pricing grid. Combined with the deferral of principal amortization and extension of debt maturity through December 2029, this transaction significantly enhances our financial flexibility as we continue executing our Monument Draw development program.” Transaction Description The New Credit Agreement amends and restates in its entirety the Second Amended and Restated Senior Secured Credit Agreement dated December 26, 2024, as amended (the “Existing Credit Agreement”). The transaction amends and restates the Existing Credit Agreement and does not involve a novation. Outstanding term loans under the Existing Credit Agreement will continue under the New Credit Agreement as Closing Date Term Loans, against a maximum Closing Date Term Loan Commitment of $162.5 million and no new cash borrowing. Key terms of the New Credit Agreement include: Interest Rate : SOFR plus a fixed applicable margin of 6.50% per annum (or ABR plus 5.50%), along with a 0.15% credit spread adjustment. The fixed margin replaces the leverage-based pricing grid under the Existing Credit Agreement, under which the SOFR margin ranged from 7.75% to 8.50% depending on the Company's Total Net Leverage Ratio. Maturity : December 31, 2029. Delayed Draw Facility : Up to $175.0 million of discretionary delayed draw term loan capacity, available on an uncommitted basis and subject to each lender's sole discretion to provide commitments. Amortization : Scheduled quarterly principal amortization commences with the fiscal quarter ending June 30, 2027. Financial Covenants : Includes maintenance covenants relating to Total Net Leverage Ratio, Current Ratio, Asset Coverage Ratio and minimum Liquidity, each commencing with the fiscal quarter ending September 30, 2026. A copy of the Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement will be filed as an exhibit to a Current Report on Form 8-K with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Forward Looking Statements This release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of Section 27A of the Securities Act of 1933, as amended, and Section 21E of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended. Statements that are not strictly historical statements constitute forward-looking statements. Forward-looking statements include, among others, statements about the expected benefits of the Third Amended and Restated Credit Agreement, anticipated improvements in the Company’s borrowing cost and financial ratios, future amortization obligations, covenant compliance expectations, the potential availability or use of the Discretionary Delayed Draw Term Loan facility, and the Company’s ability to execute its development program. Forward-looking statements can often, but not always, be identified by the use of such words as “expects”, “believes”, “intends”, “anticipates”, “plans”, “estimates”, “projects,” “potential”, “possible”, or “probable” or statements that certain actions, events or results “may”, “will”, “should”, or “could” be taken, occur or be achieved. Forward-looking statements are based on current beliefs and expectations and involve certain assumptions or estimates that involve various risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those reflected in the statements. These risks include, but are not limited to, those set forth in the Company’s Annual Report on Form 10-K for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025, and other filings submitted by the Company to the SEC, copies of which may be obtained from the SEC’s website at www.sec.gov or through the Company’s website at www.battalionoil.com. Readers should not place undue reliance on any such forward-looking statements, which are made only as of the date hereof. title: Roy Jakobs to join GSK Board as Non-Executive Director
summary: Roy Jakobs will join the Board of the Company as a Non-Executive Director from 13 July 2026.
body_text: 09 July 2026 Issued: London, UK For media and investors only Roy Jakobs to join GSK Board as Non-Executive Director Download (PDF - 139.8KB) GSK plc (LSE/NYSE: GSK) has today announced that Roy Jakobs will join the Board of the Company as a Non-Executive Director from 13 July 2026. Mr Jakobs is currently Chief Executive Officer of Royal Philips, a global leader in health technology with sales of 17.8 billion EUR in 2025 and 65,000 employees worldwide, headquartered in Amsterdam, Netherlands. Mr Jakobs has served as CEO of Royal Philips since 2022, and prior to that held international roles of increasing seniority after joining the company in 2010. Mr Jakobs has also held senior roles at other global companies including Shell and Elsevier, and holds a Master’s in Business Administration (MBA). Sir Jonathan Symonds, Chair of GSK said, “We are delighted to welcome Roy to the Board. His experience as CEO of a global health technology company, specialising in innovative adjacent technologies to biopharmaceuticals including patient monitoring, imaging, and intervention, will bring valuable perspective to Luke and the Board. Roy’s values and approach to culture and purpose are highly aligned with our own, and he is well-placed to support GSK as we focus on accelerating growth and delivering better medicines for the patients who need them and greater value for shareholders.” Notes: The appointment of Mr Jakobs was made by the Board on the recommendation of the Nominations & Corporate Governance Committee. The Board agreed a target skills matrix for the role and was assisted and supported in candidate selection and evaluation by an external search firm, which is a signatory of the Voluntary Code of Conduct for Executive Search Firms. The Board satisfied itself that Mr Jakobs had the experience and time available to carry out the role. The Board has determined that Mr Jakobs is an independent Non-Executive Director in accordance with the UK Corporate Governance Code. Mr Jakobs will receive the standard annual fee for a Non-Executive Director of £122,258. He will be required to build towards a share ownership requirement of GSK shares in accordance with the Company’s shareholder approved Non-Executive Director Remuneration policy – currently two times the standard annual fee. Mr Jakobs does not have a service contract. He has a letter of appointment which may be viewed by contacting the Company Secretary at the Company’s registered office. There are no further disclosures to be made in respect of Mr Jakobs’ appointment under Listing Rule 6.4.8R. As of 13 July 2026, the Board of GSK will comprise: Sir Jonathan Symonds CBE Non-Executive Chair Luke Miels Chief Executive Officer Julie Brown Chief Financial Officer Charles Bancroft Senior Independent Non-Executive Director Elizabeth McKee Anderson Independent Non-Executive Director Dr Hal Barron Non-Executive Director Dr Anne Beal Independent Non-Executive Director Wendy Becker CBE Independent Non-Executive Director Dr Hal Dietz Independent Non-Executive Director Mr Roy Jakobs Independent Non-Executive Director Dr Jeannie Lee Independent Non-Executive Director Dr Gavin Screaton Independent Non-Executive Director Dr Vishal Sikka Independent Non-Executive Director About GSK GSK is a global biopharma company with a purpose to unite science, technology, and talent to get ahead of disease together. Find out more at www.gsk.com . Cautionary statement regarding forward-looking statements GSK cautions investors that any forward-looking statements or projections made by GSK, including those made in this announcement, are subject to risks and uncertainties that may cause actual results to differ materially from those projected. Such factors include, but are not limited to, those described in the “Risk Factors” section in GSK’s Annual Report on Form 20-F for 2025, and GSK’s Q1 Results for 2026. title: Credit Union 1 (Alaska) expands collaboration with NCR Atleos through statewide ATM branding in Circle K stores
summary: NCR Atleos Corporation (NYSE: NATL) (“Atleos”), a leader in expanding self-service financial access for financial institutions, retailers and consumers, today announced that Credit Union 1 (CU1), headquartered in Anchorage, Alaska, is expanding its collaboration with Atleos through an ATM branding agreement at Circle K stores in Alaska, reinforcing its commitment to accessible, convenient self‑service banking for members across the state.
body_text: ATLANTA -- NCR Atleos Corporation (NYSE: NATL) (“Atleos”), a leader in expanding self-service financial access for financial institutions, retailers and consumers, today announced that Credit Union 1 (CU1), headquartered in Anchorage, Alaska, is expanding its collaboration with Atleos through an ATM branding agreement at Circle K stores in Alaska, reinforcing its commitment to accessible, convenient self‑service banking for members across the state. Under the agreement, Atleos displays Credit Union 1 branding on ATMs in 24 Circle K locations throughout Anchorage, Fairbanks, Wasilla and the Kenai Peninsula. The initiative, launching in July-August 2026, provides continuity of service while establishing a consistent and recognizable CU1 presence across high‑traffic retail locations. Credit Union 1 serves Alaskan communities statewide and manages more than $1.7 billion in assets, making it the second largest credit union in Alaska. With members spread across vast geography and diverse communities, reliable access to cash through trusted retail locations is a critical element of the credit union’s service model. Operating across one of the most geographically expansive and logistically complex environments in the world, Credit Union 1 utilizes ATM infrastructure backed by strong monitoring, fulfillment and service capabilities. NCR Atleos brings significant expertise in supporting self‑service banking at scale—even in remote and demanding environments—and provides operational services across Alaska. “Access and convenience are essential for our members, no matter where they live in Alaska,” said Mark Burgess, President/CEO of Credit Union 1. “Our collaboration with NCR Atleos and the branding agreement at Circle K in Alaska extends the reach and visibility of Credit Union 1 into the everyday places our members already visit, making it easier for them to access their financial services while they shop, fuel and travel across the state.” This agreement is one of many continued efforts that have expanded CU1's reach across Alaska, including new branch openings in Kotzebue, Wasilla and Skagway in 2025, a branch opening in Homer coming in August, and the recently approved merger with MAC Federal Credit Union. Together, these investments continue to strengthen access, convenience and service for members statewide. “Retail ATM access plays a critical role in expanding financial access across large and remote regions,” said Steven Nogalo, General Manager of North America for Atleos. “By supporting Credit Union 1’s Circle K branding initiative statewide, Atleos is helping deliver self‑service access backed by operational strength and proven service capabilities. We’re proud to deepen this relationship and help support members across Alaska.” About Atleos Atleos (NYSE: NATL) is a leader in expanding self-service financial access, with industry-leading ATM expertise and experience , unrivaled operational scale including the largest independently-owned ATM network , always-on global services and constant innovation . Atleos improves operational efficiency for financial institutions, drives footfall for retailers and enables digital-first financial self-service experiences for consumers. Atleos is ranked #12 in Newsweek’s prestigious 2025 Top 100 Global Most Loved Workplaces® list. Atleos is headquartered in Atlanta, Ga., with approximately 20,000 employees globally. For more information, visit www.ncratleos.com . title: Best Luggage Tracker 2026: GPS vs. Bluetooth Compared
summary: Enjoy and learn from Life360's blog archive, focused on user life stories and experiences with our premier family safety app.
body_text: Summary What this article covers: A clear breakdown of how luggage trackers work, the difference between GPS and Bluetooth tracking options, what to look for before you buy, and which tracker makes the most sense for your travel style. Who It's For Frequent travelers are tired of wondering where their checked luggage ends up Anyone who has dealt with lost luggage and never wants to go through it again Families packing for a big trip who want peace of mind from gate to baggage claim Android users and iPhone users are trying to figure out which tracker actually works with their phone Pet parents and families already using Life360 who want to protect their bags, too Key Takeaways Luggage trackers rely on either GPS or Bluetooth technology, and they work very differently from each other. GPS trackers tap into satellites and cellular networks for wide-area tracking. Bluetooth trackers work by pinging nearby devices and drop off once you're out of range. Battery life, airline compliance, and phone compatibility all matter before you commit to a tracker. Apple AirTag works best for Apple users. Tile works across both iOS and Android. Life360 brings everything together on one map. The best luggage tracker is the one that fits how you actually travel, not just the one with the best marketing. You packed your bags the night before and you triple-checked the zipper. You got to the airport with time to spare. Then your suitcase went somewhere entirely different. Lost luggage is one of those travel nightmares that feels impossible until it happens to you. Airlines misplace or delay millions of bags every year, and when it's your bag sitting in some unknown airport, the panic is real. A luggage tracker does not guarantee your bag arrives on time, but it does tell you exactly where it is so you can stop guessing and start doing something about it. Before you toss a luggage tracker in your bag and call it done, it helps to understand what you're actually getting. How Luggage Trackers Work Every tracker on the market communicates through a signal. The type of signal determines how far it reaches, how accurate it is, and how useful it becomes when your bag goes missing. GPS trackers tap into satellites to calculate a location, then send that data to your phone through cellular networks. This is the same technology behind turn-by-turn navigation. The location shows up on a map, updates frequently, and works across long distances. If your bag ended up in a completely different city, a GPS tracker tells you that with a clear pin on a map. Bluetooth trackers work differently. Instead of connecting to satellites, they ping nearby devices. When another smartphone running the same app passes close enough to your tracker, it picks up the signal and updates the location. Within a short distance, that works well. Once your bag is beyond Bluetooth range, usually a few hundred feet at most, you lose the real-time picture entirely. That gap in how luggage trackers work is the most important thing to understand before buying one. Your bag, your family, your stuff. One map. Life360 and Tile work together so your luggage travels on the same map as your people — no extra apps, no extra logins, no panic at baggage claim. See Life360 plans GPS Trackers vs. Bluetooth Trackers for Your Luggage The best comparison comes down to range and reliability when it matters most. What GPS Tracking Gets Right GPS trackers give you location data no matter where your bag ends up. They tap into satellites and cellular networks independently, which means distance is rarely the problem. For checked luggage that might travel through three airports before reaching yours, GPS is the stronger option. The tradeoff is size, battery life, and cost. Most GPS-based tracking devices require a monthly subscription to cover cellular data, and they tend to be bulkier than their Bluetooth counterparts. Where Bluetooth Trackers Still Shine Bluetooth trackers shine in scenarios where your bag is nearby, but you can't find it. Lost in a crowded baggage claim? A Bluetooth tracker with an audible alarm can help you locate it fast. Some devices also support precision finding, which guides you directionally toward the tracker. The limitation hits when your bag is actually lost. In low-traffic areas with few nearby devices to relay the signal, Bluetooth trackers become much less effective. The short version: GPS works better for finding truly lost luggage . Bluetooth works better for locating a closed bag that is out of sight. What to Know About Airline Rules and Airplane Mode Before you decide which tracker to bring on your next flight, this matters. Most airlines require that electronic devices with cellular connectivity be placed in airplane mode during flight . GPS trackers that use cellular networks fall into that category. Some trackers automatically detect when they're on a plane and switch into a low-power or airplane mode on their own. Others need to be manually adjusted before your flight. Bluetooth trackers generally do not transmit in a way that interferes with aircraft systems, so they're typically allowed as-is. That said, policies vary by airline, and it's worth checking before you travel. The FAA and most major carriers have warmed up to small tracking devices in recent years, but the safest approach is still to review the specific airline's policy before you pack one in your checked luggage. Battery Life and What to Expect Battery life varies quite a bit depending on the type of tracker and how actively it's updating your location. GPS Tracker Battery Life GPS trackers that run on cellular networks use more power because they're doing more work. Depending on the model and how frequently it updates, you might get anywhere from a few days to two weeks on a single charge. Some offer a low-power reserve mode that stretches the battery significantly when you're not actively tracking. If you travel often, this is worth paying close attention to because a dead tracker is just extra weight in your bag. Bluetooth Tracker Battery Life Bluetooth trackers tend to last much longer on a single battery, sometimes months. Many use a replaceable battery, which makes maintenance simple. You swap it out when needed and keep going. The tradeoff, again, is that you're trading range for longevity. Longer battery life is great. It just does not compensate for limited coverage when your bag is genuinely missing. A Look at the Most Popular Luggage Trackers Apple AirTag The AirTag is designed for Apple users and works within the Apple Find My network. It uses Bluetooth to communicate with nearby Apple devices, which relay the location back to you through the app. In areas with a high density of iPhone users, like major airports, the coverage is actually pretty solid. Precision finding is one of its standout features, using your iPhone's camera and sensors to guide you directly toward the tag. The limitation is obvious: this only works well in the Apple ecosystem. Android users get nothing from an AirTag. If your family runs a mix of iOS devices and Android devices, the AirTag only covers part of your crew. Tile and Tile Pro Tile is one of the most widely recognized names in Bluetooth tracking, and for good reason. It works across both iOS and Android , which makes it a better fit for mixed-device households. The Life360 app connects your tracker to a network of nearby Tile users who help relay location updates even if you're not close. The Tile is compact and affordable , making it easy to toss in a bag or wallet. The Tile Pro offers a longer Bluetooth range and a louder audible alarm, which comes in handy in a busy baggage claim. Both use a replaceable battery, so maintenance stays simple. Where Tile falls short is the same place all Bluetooth trackers do. In areas without many nearby devices, the network gets thin. If your luggage is sitting unattended in a storage facility or a remote airport, the signal chain can break. Everything you travel with. One place to find it all. Tile trackers inside Life360 means your bags, your family, and your pet are all on the same map — before you even board. See Life360 plans Life360 and Tile Together If you're already using Life360 to keep an eye on your family, your pet, and your important stuff, Tile trackers integrate directly into the same map. Your luggage, your keys, your bag, and your people all appear in one place without juggling multiple apps. For travel specifically, attaching a Tile to your suitcase means your whole circle can help you locate it. If someone in your Life360 circle passes near your bag, the location updates automatically. It's a quiet, practical safety net that works in the background while you focus on actually getting to your destination. Choosing the Right Tracker for Your Travel Style If you take international trips with multiple connections, GPS-based trackers offer the most reliable coverage. The wider the range, the better your chances of locating your bag, even if it ended up on the wrong continent. For domestic trips or shorter travel, Bluetooth trackers handle most real-world scenarios well enough, especially in airports where plenty of other users can relay your signal. The Tile Mate is a low-maintenance, affordable option that fits easily in checked luggage or a backpack. Android users should pay close attention to compatibility before buying. The Apple AirTag is effectively off the table for Android. Tile and Life360 work across both platforms, which makes them more flexible for households that mix smartphones. And if you travel with your whole family, your pet, and all the things that tend to go missing at once, bringing everything into the Life360 app means one less thing to manage on the road. A Few Practical Tips Before You Pack Your Tracker Attach it somewhere secure. A small loop or clip inside the main compartment works well. Avoid spots near zippers where the tracker can shift or snag. Check the battery before you leave. Charge it fully, or confirm the replaceable battery is fresh. A tracker at 10% is not going to last through a three-day delay. Set up the app at home. Troubleshooting the setup at the airport is not fun. Make sure everything is connected and tested before your trip starts. Handle airplane mode before you board. If you're using a GPS tracker, check whether it needs to be manually switched. Some handle this automatically. Others need a quick adjustment. Label your luggage clearly on the outside, too. A tracker helps you find the bag. Clear identification helps the airline reunite it with you faster once it's located. Final Thoughts For most travelers, a Bluetooth tracker like the Tile Mate or Tile Pro reliably handles everyday travel scenarios without much hassle. If you travel frequently with checked luggage on long-haul routes, GPS trackers offer wider coverage when the stakes are higher. Life360 brings it all together. Tile trackers work inside the Life360 app, so your bag, your family, and your important belongings live on one shared map. It's not just about finding lost items. It's about knowing where everything is so you can travel with a little more confidence and a lot less panic. title: AI Report 2026: How Small Businesses Are Using AI to Grow

body_text: AI Has Officially Moved Into the Mainstream A few years ago, artificial intelligence felt like something built for large companies with big budgets and dedicated technology teams. Today, it’s becoming part of everyday life for small businesses. Whether it’s helping write marketing emails, responding to customer inquiries, organizing schedules, generating social media content, or automating repetitive tasks, AI is finding its way into nearly every corner of business operations. The latest Thryv AI & Small Business Adoption Report shows just how quickly things are changing. This year, 66% of small businesses report using AI, up from 55% last year. More importantly, AI is no longer something owners are simply testing. For many, it’s become part of their daily workflow. The message from this year’s report is clear: small businesses have embraced AI. The bigger question now is how to use it more effectively. AI adoption among small businesses increased from 55% to 66% year over year. Nearly 70% of business owners say they need more AI skills and training. 70% report increased revenue from AI investments. 83% say AI saves valuable time every month. 86% view AI as an opportunity rather than a threat. AI and Small Business Adoption Report 2026 Get the inside story on how small businesses are using AI to fuel growth, the challenges they face, and what it all means for the future of small business success. Download Small Businesses Want More Than AI Tools. They Want AI Skills. While adoption continues to rise, many business owners feel they’re still learning how to get the most from the technology. In fact, nearly 70% of respondents say they lack the skills needed to use AI effectively. That finding highlights an important shift happening across the small business community. The challenge is no longer access. Business owners have access to AI tools. They’re experimenting with them. They’re seeing results. What they’re looking for now is guidance. They want to know: Which tools are worth using How to write better prompts Where AI fits into their daily workflow How to save more time without creating more complexity How to use AI strategically instead of occasionally It’s one reason so many owners are turning to webinars, online resources, social media, and even AI itself to continue learning. The businesses that invest in developing AI skills may have the greatest opportunity to gain a competitive advantage over the next few years. AI Is Helping Small Businesses Do More With Less Small business owners have always been experts at wearing multiple hats. Marketing manager. Salesperson. Customer service representative. Bookkeeper. Operations manager. Now AI is helping lighten some of that workload. One of the report’s most interesting findings shows that if AI software and a new employee could perform the same task equally well, nearly half of business owners would choose AI. That doesn’t mean owners are replacing employees with technology. Instead, they’re using AI to extend the capacity of their existing teams. When labor costs continue to rise and hiring remains challenging in many industries, AI offers a practical way to increase productivity without increasing headcount. For many businesses, it serves as an extra set of hands that never clocks out. The ROI Story Is Becoming Hard to Ignore For years, discussions about AI focused on possibilities. Today, business owners are increasingly focused on results. And according to this year’s report, many are finding them. Among businesses currently using AI: 70% say it has increased revenue 55% say it has reduced costs 83% say it saves time 81% say it helps them make more strategic decisions For small business owners, time is often the most valuable resource of all. The majority of AI users report saving anywhere from 11 to 40 hours each month. That’s time that can be spent following up with leads, serving customers, improving operations, or focusing on growth initiatives that often get pushed aside during busy weeks. The takeaway isn’t that AI replaces work. It’s that AI helps create more time for the work that matters most. 4 AI Checklists to Automate and Grow Your Small Business Simplify your daily operations with practical AI checklists designed to save time, improve consistency, and help you scale with confidence. From CRM and content to dashboards and customer interactions, learn how to streamline the systems that power your business. Download Customers Are Changing Their Expectations Today’s consumers expect businesses to respond faster, communicate more personally, and deliver a smoother overall experience. Meeting those expectations can be difficult for small businesses with limited staff and resources. That’s where AI is increasingly making a difference. According to the report: 72% believe AI is necessary for acquiring new customers 68% say it helps them meet rising customer expectations More than half worry they could lose customers if they fail to adopt AI Many small business owners are discovering that AI isn’t just improving efficiency behind the scenes. It’s helping create better customer experiences at every stage of the customer journey. Small Businesses Continue to See Opportunity in AI Despite concerns often highlighted in media headlines, most small business owners remain optimistic. An overwhelming 86% say they view AI as an opportunity rather than a threat. That optimism likely comes from experience. Business owners are seeing firsthand how AI can help solve everyday challenges, from managing workloads and improving marketing performance to responding to customers faster and making smarter decisions. Rather than viewing AI as a replacement for people, many see it as a tool that helps people work more effectively. What These Findings Mean for Small Businesses If there is one lesson from this year’s report, it’s that AI adoption is no longer the differentiator. Implementation is. The businesses seeing the greatest results aren’t necessarily using the most advanced tools. They’re finding practical ways to apply AI to real business challenges. They’re saving time. They’re improving customer experiences. They’re operating more efficiently. And they’re creating capacity to focus on growth. As AI continues to evolve, the businesses that combine technology with the right processes and strategy will be best positioned to stay competitive. How Thryv Helps Small Businesses Put AI to Work The promise of AI isn’t just about automation. It’s about helping small business owners spend less time managing tasks and more time growing their business. Thryv helps make that possible. From creating marketing content and managing customer communications to organizing leads and automating follow-up, Thryv’s AI-powered tools help small businesses simplify daily operations and improve efficiency. Because when AI is built into the tools you already use, it’s easier to turn potential into results. And that’s where the real value begins. title: Macro Scenarios in Focus: Central-Bank Credibility and Portfolio Risk
summary: Weakening Federal Reserve credibility could fuel stagflation. We model three macroeconomic scenarios and their impact on a multi-asset-class portfolio.
body_text: Key findings The Federal Reserve’s credibility may emerge as a key macro risk, increasing the likelihood of stagflation, with sticky inflation and slow growth. We provide a framework for multi-asset-class investors to assess portfolio impacts under three potential 2026 macroeconomic scenarios: stagflation, recession and stable growth. We show how these scenarios translate into various outcomes for a multi-asset-class portfolio, with returns ranging from an 11% loss under stagflation to a 4% gain under a stable-growth outlook. Market confidence in the Federal Reserve’s independence may prove decisive in 2026. With inflation still above target and emerging signs of a softer labor market, pressure to ease policy risks colliding with the Fed’s mandate.1 Federal Reserve Chair Jerome Powell's grand-jury subpoenas on Jan. 9 — and published video response on Jan. 11 — further added to the already-delicate policy backdrop. When central-bank credibility erodes, inflation can persist even as growth slows — creating stagflation, in which bonds fail to diversify equities.2 In our stagflation scenario, a global diversified portfolio could lose roughly 11%. By contrast, a recession with falling yields could limit losses to around 5% through bond gains, while a productivity-led soft landing could deliver a 4% return. Why Fed credibility matters Political pressure in 2025 put Fed independence and credibility under scrutiny.3 When central-bank credibility weakens, inflation becomes harder to control through monetary policy, because shocks are more likely to persist and expectations become less anchored. Central-bank credibility is reflected through inflation persistence within the MSCI Macro-Finance Model , as shown in the chart below. Think of it as stickiness: When credibility is high (parameter near 0), inflation snaps back to its long-term average quickly. When credibility erodes (parameter near 1), today’s inflation bleeds into tomorrow’s.4 Credibility was low in the 1970s, when inflation shocks lingered and expectations drifted higher. It strengthened during the Volcker disinflation, as decisive tightening re-anchored expectations, and remained high through the Great Moderation from the mid-1980s to 2007, when inflation shocks tended to fade quickly.5 After the COVID-19 surge in prices, credibility weakened again as markets questioned whether monetary policy was sufficiently tight to bring inflation back to target. Looking ahead, policy decisions that ease financial conditions while inflation remains above target could similarly affect expectations and prolong the persistence of inflation shocks. Weaker central-bank credibility coincided with higher inflation Inflation and the policy rate (top panel) and inflation persistence (bottom panel). Inflation persistence is bounded between 0 and 1: Higher inflation persistence corresponds to weaker credibility and slower mean reversion. Source: Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development, Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis FRED database, MSCI Three forward-looking macroeconomic scenarios Using the MSCI Macro-Finance Analyzer , we refreshed our three scenarios with more recent market data, interpreting the stagflation narrative through the lens of weakened central-bank credibility.6 The stagflation scenario is characterized by an initial inflation shock and a sharp rise in long-term Treasury yields, as inflation expectations de-anchor. Inflation remains persistent and growth is sluggish in the medium term. By contrast, in the recession scenario, a reduction in economic activity weakens labor demand and pulls inflation lower. Treasury yields decline as the Fed shifts toward rate cuts. Stronger productivity growth and resilient consumption support economic activity in the stable-outlook scenario. Growth receives a near-term boost, and inflation converges back toward target. Growth and inflation under our scenarios GDP and inflation paths were generated with the MSCI Macro-Finance Analyzer, using the MSCI baseline scenario as of June 30, 2025. These are not forecasts, but hypothetical narratives of different macroeconomic scenarios. Impact on multi-asset-class portfolios To assess the scenarios’ impact on multi-asset-class portfolios, we used MSCI’s predictive stress-testing framework and applied the shocks from the table below to a hypothetical global diversified portfolio, consisting of global equities, U.S. bonds and real estate.7 Broad market shocks under our scenarios Assumptions about risk-factor shocks are informed by the MSCI Macro-Finance Analyzer and by analysis of historical data and judgment. Breakeven inflation (BEI) is measured in basis points (bps). This is not a forecast, but a hypothetical narrative of how the scenario could affect multi-asset-class portfolios. Portfolio returns show that diversification depends on the macro regime. When inflation persists and policy credibility is questioned, bonds may no longer hedge equity risk, leading to the most severe losses, under stagflation: Equities and bonds sell off, and the portfolio falls by about 11%. In the recession scenario, the drawdown is materially smaller (5%) as declining yields allow bonds to offset equity losses. Under a stable outlook, the portfolio delivers a gain of 4%. Stagflation worst outcome for our portfolio Loading chart... Please wait. Portfolio impact of the scenario based on market data as of Dec. 19, 2025. Source: S&P Global Market Intelligence, MSCI Positioning portfolios for the policy environment For investors, the key question is not only where inflation and growth will go — but whether the Fed can keep expectations anchored. A shift in credibility could alter cross-asset-class correlations and redefine portfolio risks in the year ahead. The author thanks John Burke and William Baker for their contributions to this blog post. body_text: View all news Solid Power Appoints Uwe Breitweg to Board of Directors, Adding Deep Automotive and Battery Strategy Expertise 07/01/2026 Download (opens in new window) Mr. Breitweg brings more than two decades of automotive leadership, with deep expertise in battery strategy, powertrain development, and vehicle engineering Appointment made pursuant to BMW Holding B.V.'s director nomination rights LOUISVILLE, Colo.--(BUSINESS WIRE)-- Solid Power, Inc. (Nasdaq: SLDP), a leading U.S.-based developer of solid-state battery technology, today announced the appointment of Uwe Breitweg, Vice President Powertrain, Emission and Battery Strategy of the BMW Group, to its board of directors, effective July 1, 2026. His appointment underscores BMW continuing to work very closely together with Solid Power as a strategic development partner in this future key technology. "Mr. Breitweg brings to Solid Power an exceptional combination of technical depth and strategic leadership across battery and vehicle engineering at one of the world's premier automotive companies," said John Van Scoter, President and CEO of Solid Power. "His perspective will be invaluable as we continue to advance our solid-state technology and execute our strategy with automotive and cell manufacturing partners around the world. On behalf of the entire board, I welcome him to the team. I would also like to thank Dr. Feurer for his dedicated service and many contributions to Solid Power during his tenure on the board." Mr. Breitweg has more than two decades of leadership experience in the global automotive industry, with deep expertise in battery strategy, powertrain development, and vehicle engineering. He currently serves as Vice President Powertrain, Emission and Battery Strategy for the BMW Group, a role he has held since 2021. Previously, he served as Vice President Powertrain Systems Industrial Customers from 2016 to 2021 at the BMW Group. About Solid Power, Inc. Solid Power is developing solid-state battery technology to enable the next generation of batteries for the fast-growing EV and other markets. Solid Power’s core technology is its electrolyte material, which Solid Power believes can enable extended driving range, longer battery life, improved safety, and lower cost compared to traditional lithium-ion. Solid Power’s business model – selling its electrolyte to cell manufacturers and licensing its cell designs and manufacturing processes – distinguishes the company from many of its competitors who plan to be commercial battery manufacturers. Ultimately, Solid Power endeavors to be a leading producer and distributor of sulfide-based solid electrolyte material for powering both EVs and other applications. For more information, visit http://www.solidpowerbattery.com/ . title: Rigetti Computing to Report Second Quarter 2026 Financial Results and Host Conference Call on August 6, 2026
summary: BERKELEY, Calif., July 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rigetti Computing, Inc. ("Rigetti" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: RGTI), a pioneer in hybrid quantum-classical computing, announced today that it will release second quarter 2026 results on Thursday, August 6, 2026, after market close.
body_text: BERKELEY, Calif., July 23, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Rigetti Computing, Inc. ("Rigetti" or the "Company") (Nasdaq: RGTI), a pioneer in hybrid quantum-classical computing, announced today that it will release second quarter 2026 results on Thursday, August 6, 2026, after market close. The Company will host a conference call to discuss its financial results and provide an update on its business operations at 5:00 p.m. ET the same day. Key details regarding the call are as follows: Call Date: Thursday, August 6, 2026 Call Time: 5:00 p.m. ET / 2:00 p.m. PT Webcast Link: https://edge.media-server.com/mmc/p/9pedzvky Live Call Participant Link: https://register-conf.media-server.com/register/BI6483c92f267f4169a6d27a72dc7c5e58 Webcast Instructions You can listen to a live audio webcast of the conference call by visiting the “Webcast Link” above or the "Events & Presentations" section of the Company's Investor Relations website at https://investors.rigetti.com/. A replay of the conference call will be available at the same locations following the conclusion of the call for one year. Live Call Participant Instructions To participate in the live call, you must register using the “Live Call Participant Link” above. Once registered, you will receive dial-in numbers and a unique PIN number. When you dial in, you will input your PIN and be routed into the call. If you register and forget your PIN, or lose the registration confirmation email, simply re-register to receive a new PIN. About Rigetti Rigetti is a pioneer in full-stack quantum computing. Rigetti quantum computers are based on superconducting qubits, which are widely believed to be the leading qubit modality given their maturity, clear path to scaling, and fast gate speeds. Rigetti quantum computing systems achieve gate speeds of 50-70 nanoseconds, which is about 1,000 times faster than alternative modalities such as trapped-ion and neutral-atom systems. Rigetti sells on-premises 9-qubit to 108-qubit quantum computing systems, which support national laboratories and quantum computing centers. Rigetti’s Cepheus 36-qubit to 108-qubit systems are based on the Company’s proprietary chiplet-based technology and include the Company’s control electronics. Rigetti’s 9-qubit Novera QPU supports a broader R&D community with a high-performance, on-premises QPU designed to plug into a customer’s existing cryogenic and control systems. The Company operates quantum computers over the cloud through its Rigetti Quantum Cloud Services (QCS) platform, enabling global enterprise, government, and research clients to pursue R&D. The Company’s proprietary quantum-classical infrastructure provides high-performance integration with public and private clouds for practical quantum computing. Rigetti developed the industry’s first multi-chip quantum processor for scalable quantum computing systems. Leveraging this proprietary technology, Rigetti deployed the industry’s largest multi-chip quantum computer in 2026 with Cepheus-1-108Q, based on twelve 9-qubit chiplets tiled together. The Company designs and manufactures its chips in-house at Fab-1, the industry’s first dedicated and integrated quantum device manufacturing facility. Learn more at https://www.rigetti.com/ . Rigetti Computing Media Contact: press@rigetti.com Rigetti Computing Investor Relations Contact: IR@rigetti.com
